system:
You audit the knowledge atoms of one Knowledge Card. A card is the answer key for a benchmark of expert conceptual knowledge, so every atom must be correct, self-contained, and assessable on its own.

Judge every atom on every check listed below. Rules:
- For checks about evidence, use only the evidence sentences supplied with the atom. Do not repair an atom with your own knowledge.
- Evidence text comes from a PDF text layer. If symbols are garbled so that you cannot verify the atom, answer "hold" for that check and say so.
- Be strict. When unsure between pass and a non-pass value, choose the non-pass value and explain.
- "why" is required for every value other than the first listed value; keep it under 30 words. Omit "why" when passing.

Checks (allowed values in brackets; the first value means no problem):
- GROUNDED [pass / revise / fail]: The cited evidence sentences state the atom. pass = fully stated. revise = the core claim is stated, and the gap is only wording, strength, or a dropped/extra peripheral qualifier that can be fixed by deleting or softening words (say what). fail = not stated, OR the atom adds substantive content the evidence lacks: a scope or population restriction (e.g. 'In B-ALL'), a mechanism or operation, a characterization (e.g. 'an unbounded while loop'), or a formula/definition. If deleting the unsupported part would change what the atom tests, it is fail, not revise. For pass, put the supporting evidence ids in cite (required).
- SINGLE_CLAIM [pass / revise]: The atom is one independently assessable claim. revise = it joins two or more claims that could be true or false separately.
- SCOPE_LABEL [pass / revise]: The S label fits (S1 what it is / S2 how it works / S3 where it ends). revise = wrong label; put the right one in why, e.g. 'S2: ...'.
- L1_ONLY [pass / revise / fail]: The atom is recall-level knowledge: one fact a person who studied the concept would simply know. revise = the core fact is recall-level but the sentence carries extra load that must be removed, e.g. stacked conditions (since/although/if ... and ...), a procedural or evaluative add-on ('easy to define but requires checking ...'), or a clause that introduces a second technical concept that must be known separately (e.g. 'if X is an inner Kan complex' when that is not the card concept). fail = knowing it requires applying the concept to a new problem, or combining facts from distant passages.
- SOURCE_INDEPENDENT [pass / revise / fail]: A domain expert who never read this book could judge the claim true or false. revise = phrased as the authors' statement but the claim itself is general (drop the attribution). fail = the authors' opinion or choice, or the finding of one study, so the answer is not fixed without the source.
- NO_OVERLAP [pass / fail]: No other atom in this card states or contains the same claim. If two atoms overlap, fail only the less informative one and put the other atom's id in cite; the other one passes.
- CENTRALITY [pass / fail]: The atom matters for understanding the concept. fail = peripheral detail.
Whole-card checks (report under "batch"):
- CONCEPT_SCOPE [pass / fail]: The concept is a general concept of the field. fail = a single system, product, or one study's topic.

Output ONLY one JSON object:
{"units": {"<atom_id>": {"<CHECK>": {"v": "<value>", "why": "", "cite": []}, ...}, ...}, "batch": {"<CHECK>": {"v": "<value>", "why": ""}}}
user:
CONCEPT: Reedy model structure
ASSESSMENT SCOPE: Reedy categories (degree function, positive/negative morphisms, with automorphisms), matching and latching maps, Reedy (trivial) fibrations/cofibrations, existence of the model structure and comparison with projective, and application to simplicial objects and realizations.

ATOMS:
- HMDEND-C08-S1-01 | S1
  ATOM: A Reedy category is a category R equipped with a degree function $d:\mathrm{ob}(R)\to\mathbb{N}$ and subcategories $R^+$ (positive) and $R^-$ (negative) of morphisms, such that every morphism factors as $f=p\circ n$ with $p$ positive and $n$ negative, uniquely up to isomorphism.
  EVIDENCE:
    [HMDEND-p0437-s04] Definition 10.1 A Reedy category is a category R equipped with the following structure:
    [HMDEND-p0437-s05] • a function d : ob(R) →N, called the degree function, • two subcategories R+ and R−, called the subcategories of positive and of negative
    [HMDEND-p0437-s08] (a) Every morphism f : r →s can be factored as f = p ◦n, where p is positive and
    [HMDEND-p0437-s09] n is negative, and this factorization is unique up to isomorphism.
- HMDEND-C08-S1-02 | S1
  ATOM: For a Reedy category R and a map Y→X of E-valued presheaves, the map Y is a Reedy (trivial) fibration if, for each object r of R, the matching map $Y(r)\to Y(\partial r)\times_{X(\partial r)}X(r)$ is a (trivial) fibration in E, where $X(\partial r)$ is the limit of X over strictly positive morphisms into r.
  EVIDENCE:
    [HMDEND-p0440-s03] Call a morphism r →s in R strictly positive if it is positive and not an isomorphism.
    [HMDEND-p0440-s05] where the limit ranges over all strictly positive morphisms into r.
    [HMDEND-p0440-s12] Definition 10.7 A map Y →X in ERop is called a Reedy (trivial) fibration if for each object r in R, the matching map above is a (trivial) fibration in E.
- HMDEND-C08-S1-03 | S1
  ATOM: In a Reedy category, positive morphisms do not decrease degree and negative morphisms do not increase degree, each strictly unless the morphism is an isomorphism, and every isomorphism is both positive and negative.
  EVIDENCE:
    [HMDEND-p0437-s10] (b) If f : r →s belongs to R+ then d(r) ≤d(s).
    [HMDEND-p0437-s11] This inequality is strict unless f
    [HMDEND-p0437-s12] is an isomorphism. Similarly, if f : r →s belongs to R−then d(r) ≥d(s) and moreover d(r) > d(s) unless f is an isomorphism.
    [HMDEND-p0437-s13] (c) Conversely, any isomorphism is both positive and negative.
- HMDEND-C08-S2-01 | S2
  ATOM: For a cofibrantly generated model category E and a Reedy category R, the presheaf category $E^{R^{op}}$ carries a cofibrantly generated model structure whose fibrations are the Reedy fibrations and whose weak equivalences are the objectwise weak equivalences, which coincide with the projective weak equivalences.
  EVIDENCE:
    [HMDEND-p0444-s11] Theorem 10.14 Let E be a cofibrantly generated model category and let R be a Reedy category.
    [HMDEND-p0444-s12] Then the category ERop of E-valued presheaves on R carries a cofibrantly generated model structure in which the fibrations are the Reedy fibrations and the weak equivalences are those maps X →Y such that X(r) →Y(r) is a weak equivalence for every r in R.
    [HMDEND-p0444-s13] In other words, they coincide with the projective weak equivalences.
- HMDEND-C08-S2-02 | S2
  ATOM: A morphism U→V in $E^{R^{op}}$ is a (trivial) Reedy cofibration if and only if for each object r the latching map $U(r)\cup_{\deg(U)(r)}\deg(V)(r)\to V(r)$ is a (trivial) cofibration in the projective model structure on $E^{\mathrm{Aut}(r)}$, where $\deg(U)(r)$ is the colimit of U(s) over strictly negative morphisms out of r.
  EVIDENCE:
    [HMDEND-p0445-s08] In order to state it, we define for an E-valued presheaf U on R and an object r ∈R an ‘object of degenerate elements’
    [HMDEND-p0445-s09] where the colimit ranges over all strictly negative morphisms out of r.
    [HMDEND-p0445-s14] U(r) ∪deg(U)(r) deg(V)(r) →V(r),
    [HMDEND-p0445-s16] Proposition 10.15 A morphism U →V in ERop is a (trivial) cofibration in the Reedy model structure of Theorem 10.14 if and only if for each object r in R, the latching map is a (trivial) cofibration in the projective model structure on EAut(r).
- HMDEND-C08-S2-03 | S2
  ATOM: A Reedy fibration $Y\to X$ is a Reedy trivial fibration if and only if $Y(r)\to X(r)$ is a weak equivalence in $\mathcal{E}$ for every object $r$ of $R$.
  EVIDENCE:
    [HMDEND-p0442-s09] (ii) If Y →X is a Reedy fibration, then it is a Reedy trivial fibration if and only if
    [HMDEND-p0442-s10] Y(r) →X(r) is a weak equivalence in E for every r in R.
- HMDEND-C08-S3-01 | S3
  ATOM: If colimits in E are universal and the cofibrations of E are precisely the monomorphisms, then the Reedy cofibrations in simplicial objects sE are precisely the monomorphisms, so the Reedy and injective model structures coincide on sE.
  EVIDENCE:
    [HMDEND-p0449-s10] Corollary 10.20 Suppose that colimits in E are universal and that the cofibrations of the model structure on E are precisely the monomorphisms.
    [HMDEND-p0449-s11] Then the same is true for the Reedy model structure on sE.
    [HMDEND-p0450-s03] Thus Corollary 10.20 can be interpreted as saying that if colimits in E are universal and the cofibrations of the model structure on E are precisely the monomorphisms, then the Reedy and injective model structures coincide on sE.
- HMDEND-C08-S3-02 | S3
  ATOM: If the projective model structure on each $E^{\mathrm{Aut}(r)}$ exists, the Reedy model structure can still be obtained without E being cofibrantly generated, and in particular when every object of the Reedy category has a trivial automorphism group the cofibrant generation assumption on E becomes redundant, though the resulting structure might not be cofibrantly generated if E is not.
  EVIDENCE:
    [HMDEND-p0447-s25] This applies in particular to Reedy categories in which the
    [HMDEND-p0448-s01] automorphism group of each object is trivial, in which case the assumption that E is cofibrantly generated becomes redundant.
    [HMDEND-p0448-s02] The Reedy model structure will then exist generally; of course, it might not be cofibrantly generated if E is not.
- HMDEND-C08-S3-03 | S3
  ATOM: Every Reedy (trivial) fibration in $E^{R^{op}}$ is a (trivial) fibration in the projective model structure, whereas the Reedy model structure has more cofibrations than the projective one while having the same weak equivalences.
  EVIDENCE:
    [HMDEND-p0444-s02] Corollary 10.12 Every Reedy (trivial) fibration in ERop is a (trivial) fibration in the projective model structure.
    [HMDEND-p0437-s02] In particular, these model structures will have more cofibrations than the projective model structure.
    [HMDEND-p0437-s03] The weak equivalences will remain the same.
